audience: Israel — and anyone hearing creation’s beginning
setting: God is creating the heavens and the earth from nothing — speaking light, order, and life into being.

about: The serpent, Eve, Adam, and the Lord God
audience: Adam and Eve in the garden — and all of us after the fall
setting: In Eden, the serpent tempts Eve and Adam; sin enters the world and fellowship with God is broken.

about: The Lord, speaking through Moses’ account of Noah
audience: Noah’s household — and every generation under God’s promise
setting: The world is filled with violence; God saves Noah’s family through the flood and makes a covenant.

audience: Abram
setting: God calls Abram to leave home for a land He will show him; promise and blessing for the nations begin.

audience: Abraham (and Isaac beside him)
setting: God tests Abraham; Isaac is nearly offered on Moriah, then God provides a ram.

audience: Moses at the burning bush
setting: At the burning bush, the Lord calls Moses to free Israel from Egypt.

audience: Israel at the Red Sea
setting: Israel is trapped at the sea; God parts the waters and overthrows Egypt’s army.

audience: Israel at Sinai
setting: At Sinai, God speaks the Ten Commandments to Israel as covenant law.

audience: Joshua
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Charge to Joshua — spoken by The Lord to Joshua.

audience: Israel remembering kindness and redemption
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Ruth and Boaz — spoken by The narrator of Ruth to Israel remembering kindness and redemption.

audience: Samuel in the Lord’s house
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Samuel hears God — spoken by The Lord (and young Samuel) to Samuel in the Lord’s house.

audience: Israel facing Goliath — and anyone facing a giant fear
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: David and Goliath — spoken by David (and the narrator) to Israel facing Goliath — and anyone facing a giant fear.

audience: David
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Davidic covenant — spoken by Nathan the prophet (from the Lord) to David.

about: The narrator of Job (and the Lord in heaven’s counsel)
audience: Readers watching Job’s trial begin
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Job’s testing begins — spoken by The narrator of Job (and the Lord in heaven’s counsel) to Readers watching Job’s trial begin.

audience: Job
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: God answers Job — spoken by The Lord to Job.

audience: Anyone who needs a Shepherd
setting: David sings of the Lord as his shepherd who leads, restores, protects through the valley, and prepares a table — goodness and mercy all his days.

audience: God — and any heart needing mercy after failure
setting: After Nathan confronts David about Bathsheba, David pleads for mercy, a clean heart, and restored joy.

audience: Those who dwell in the secret place of the Most High
setting: A hymn of refuge under the shadow of the Almighty — protection for those who dwell in the secret place of the Most High.

about: A psalm writer devoted to God’s Word
audience: Anyone learning to walk by Scripture
setting: The great acrostic love-song to God’s Word — law, precepts, and path for the pilgrim who walks by Scripture.

audience: A son (and every reader seeking guidance)
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Trust in the Lord — spoken by Solomon giving wisdom to A son (and every reader seeking guidance).

audience: Weary Judah — and anyone waiting on the Lord
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Comfort and renewed strength — spoken by Isaiah (comfort from God) to Weary Judah — and anyone waiting on the Lord.

audience: Israel — and all who look to the Suffering Servant
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Suffering Servant — spoken by Isaiah to Israel — and all who look to the Suffering Servant.

audience: The exiles in Babylon
setting: Kings reject the word; false prophets promise peace; Jeremiah sends a letter to the first exiles.

audience: Readers watching faith in the fire
setting: Three friends refuse to bow to the image and are thrown into the fiery furnace.

audience: Readers watching prayer under pressure
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Daniel in the lions’ den — spoken by The narrator of Daniel to Readers watching prayer under pressure.

about: The narrator of Jonah (and the Lord speaking)
audience: Jonah — and anyone running from mercy
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Jonah and Nineveh — spoken by The narrator of Jonah (and the Lord speaking) to Jonah — and anyone running from mercy.

audience: His disciples on the mount (and you today)
setting: Jesus teaches the Sermon on the Mount: heart righteousness, prayer, and the narrow way.

audience: His disciples who worry about tomorrow
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Do not be anxious — spoken by Jesus to His disciples who worry about tomorrow.

audience: The weary and heavy laden
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Come unto Me — spoken by Jesus to The weary and heavy laden.

audience: The disciples in the boat
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Walking on the water — spoken by Jesus (and Matthew’s account) to The disciples in the boat.

audience: The disciples — and all nations
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Last Supper, Gethsemane, trial, cross, and resurrection — spoken by The risen Jesus (through Matthew) to The disciples — and all nations.

audience: His fearful disciples in the storm
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Peace, be still — spoken by Jesus to His fearful disciples in the storm.

audience: The disciples — and the little children brought to Him
setting: Parents bring little children to Jesus; the disciples rebuke them; Jesus is much displeased and welcomes the children into His arms.

audience: His disciples learning faith and prayer
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Faith and prayer — spoken by Jesus to His disciples learning faith and prayer.

audience: Mary
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Annunciation — spoken by Gabriel (and ultimately God) to Mary.

audience: Shepherds — and all who hear of Jesus’ birth
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Nativity — spoken by Luke (and the angels’ word) to Shepherds — and all who hear of Jesus’ birth.

audience: A lawyer testing Him — and every neighbor-watcher
setting: On the road to Jerusalem: Good Samaritan, Lord’s Prayer, lost sheep/coin/son, rich fool, Zacchaeus.

audience: Sinners drawing near — and Pharisees listening
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Lost sheep, coin, and son — spoken by Jesus to Sinners drawing near — and Pharisees listening.

audience: His disciples in Gethsemane
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Gethsemane — spoken by Jesus to His disciples in Gethsemane.

audience: Readers meeting the Word made flesh
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Prologue — spoken by John the apostle to Readers meeting the Word made flesh.

audience: Nicodemus (and every seeker of new birth)
setting: At night in Jerusalem, Jesus teaches Nicodemus that new birth by the Spirit and faith in the lifted-up Son bring eternal life.

audience: The woman at the well — and her town
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Living water — spoken by Jesus to The woman at the well — and her town.

audience: His hearers — sheep who know His voice
setting: Conflict at feasts in Jerusalem; the man born blind; the Good Shepherd.

audience: Martha, Mary, and those at Lazarus’ tomb
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Lazarus raised — spoken by Jesus to Martha, Mary, and those at Lazarus’ tomb.

audience: His disciples the night before the cross
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Upper room comfort — spoken by Jesus to His disciples the night before the cross.

audience: His disciples abiding in Him
setting: Upper room: footwashing, comfort, true vine, and high priestly prayer the night before the cross.

audience: Readers standing near Jesus’ death
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Arrest, trials, crucifixion; “It is finished.” — spoken by John (witness of the cross) to Readers standing near Jesus’ death.

audience: Mary, the disciples, and Thomas — and you who believe
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Resurrection appearances — spoken by The risen Jesus (through John) to Mary, the disciples, and Thomas — and you who believe.

audience: Theophilus — and the waiting church
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Ascension — spoken by Luke to Theophilus — and the waiting church.

audience: Jerusalem at Pentecost
setting: Jesus ascends; the Spirit falls at Pentecost; the church is born in Jerusalem.

audience: Saul of Tarsus
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Paul’s conversion — spoken by The risen Jesus (and Luke’s account) to Saul of Tarsus.

audience: Readers watching faith in prison
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Philippi jail — spoken by Luke (with Paul and Silas) to Readers watching faith in prison.

audience: Believers in Rome (and you today)
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Letter to Rome — spoken by Paul to Believers in Rome (and you today).

audience: Believers learning life in the Spirit
setting: Paul teaches believers in Rome about life in the Spirit: no condemnation, adoption, and God working all things for good for those who love Him.

audience: The church at Corinth learning real love
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Love chapter — spoken by Paul to The church at Corinth learning real love.

audience: Believers holding the resurrection
setting: The resurrection of Christ and of the dead; final instructions and greetings.

audience: The church at Corinth in affliction
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: God of all comfort — spoken by Paul to The church at Corinth in affliction.

audience: Believers learning strength in weakness
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Thorn and grace — spoken by Paul to Believers learning strength in weakness.

audience: The churches of Galatia
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Freedom in Christ — spoken by Paul to The churches of Galatia.

audience: Believers putting on God’s armor
setting: Walk worthy: unity, purity, marriage, and the armor of God against spiritual war.

audience: the church at Philippi (and you today)
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Letter from prison — spoken by Paul to the church at Philippi (and you today).

audience: Believers learning prayer instead of worry
setting: Paul writes from prison to Philippi: rejoice, do not be anxious, the peace of God guards hearts; contentment in every state through Christ.

audience: Believers setting their minds above
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Life hidden with Christ — spoken by Paul to Believers setting their minds above.

audience: Believers grieving with hope
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Comfort in Christ’s coming — spoken by Paul to Believers grieving with hope.

audience: Timothy (and every timid heart)
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Spirit of power and love — spoken by Paul to Timothy (and every timid heart).

audience: Hebrew believers holding faith
setting: Hall of faith; run with patience; practical holiness and praise.

audience: Believers running with patience
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Cloud of witnesses — spoken by The writer of Hebrews to Believers running with patience.

audience: Scattered believers under trial
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Faith under pressure — spoken by James to Scattered believers under trial.

audience: Believers casting care on God
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Humble under God’s hand — spoken by Peter to Believers casting care on God.

audience: Beloved children learning God’s love
setting: Love one another; test the spirits; God is love; victory that overcomes the world.

audience: The seven churches — and every reader
setting: In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Revelation opening — spoken by John (from Jesus Christ) to The seven churches — and every reader.

audience: The church hoping for the new creation
setting: Christ returns; new heaven and new earth; the river of life; “Even so, come, Lord Jesus.”.

audience: Anyone in trouble who needs a refuge
setting: When the earth shakes and nations rage, this psalm declares God is a present refuge and strength — “be still, and know that I am God.”

audience: Worshipers giving thanks for God’s works
setting: A Sabbath song of thanksgiving in Israel’s worship: the psalmist praises the Lord because His works make the heart glad, the wicked will not last, and the righteous still flourish in old age.

audience: All lands called to joyful worship
setting: A call for all lands to enter the Lord’s gates with thanksgiving and His courts with praise.

audience: Anyone fighting fear with faith
setting: David faces fear of enemies and waits on the Lord as his light and salvation.

audience: Anyone tasting that the Lord is good — and the brokenhearted
setting: David, after escaping Abimelech, teaches: the Lord is near to the brokenhearted and saves those of a contrite spirit.

audience: Anyone who needs to know they are fully known by God
setting: David marvels that God searches him, knows him fully, formed him in the womb, and leads him in the everlasting way.

audience: Anyone whose soul is downcast
setting: Sons of Korah: a downcast soul thirsts for God and talks itself back toward hope.

audience: Travelers and anyone needing help from the Lord
setting: A song of ascents for travelers: help comes from the Lord who made heaven and earth and never sleeps.

audience: the church at Philippi (and you today)
setting: Paul writes from prison to Philippi: rejoice, do not be anxious, the peace of God guards hearts; contentment in every state through Christ.

audience: the church at Corinth facing temptation (and you today)
setting: Paul warns Corinth from Israel’s wilderness failures and promises God is faithful in temptation.

audience: His disciples — and all who guard the vulnerable
setting: In Capernaum Jesus teaches humility with a child in their midst and warns against despising little ones whose angels behold the Father’s face.

audience: Peter and the disciples learning how far forgiveness goes
setting: Peter asks how often to forgive; Jesus answers seventy times seven and tells the parable of the unforgiving servant.

audience: Believers learning kindness after the old life
setting: Paul urges the church to put off bitterness and be kind and forgiving to one another, as God in Christ forgave them.

audience: Believers putting on love as God’s chosen ones
setting: Paul tells the Colossians to put on mercy and forbear one another, forgiving as Christ forgave them.

audience: Fearful people — and you when fear is loud
setting: The Lord comforts fearful Israel in exile: “Fear thou not; for I am with thee” — strength and help from His right hand.

audience: Believers casting care on God under pressure
setting: Peter closes his letter: humble yourselves under God’s hand, cast all your care on Him, for He cares for you, and resist the devil.
